samples.summary: Unrequested scope: compactCell now preserves the four spill fields, changing behavior for every existing caller (setStyle at sheet.ts:3682, the checkbox toggle path at :3926, cellFromInput) — not part of the issue's change list (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md lists only getActiveDecimalState, unsetRangeStyleValues, changeDecimals, tests, sheet-style.md) and not recorded in any design doc (sheet-style.md's new section is silent about spill; docs/design/sheets/calculator.md owns spill semantics). It looks like a genuine latent bug fix, but it rides in unannounced and unregression-tested, so a reader of the issue cannot tell why cell payloads changed shape.

samples.summary: Asymmetry with the operation it claims to invert: the design doc calls unsetRangeStyleValues 'the reverse of setRangeStyle', but setRangeStyle's column/row/all branches operate on a single `getRangeOrActiveCell()` range (sheet.ts:3699/3712/3724), while unsetRangeStyleValues uses selectionTargets() (all of `this.ranges`) for those same layers. For a multi-range column/row selection the unset can touch layers the corresponding set would never have written, so the pair is not strictly inverse — worth either aligning or documenting.
samples.evidence: setRangeStyle column branch: `const range = this.getRangeOrActiveCell();` vs new `selectionTargets()` used for colStyles/rowStyles/sheetStyle in unsetRangeStyleValues.

It also names the API `unsetRangeStyleKeys` (line 27) where the shipped method is `unsetRangeStyleValues`. Stale in-repo documentation of the very mechanism being changed.

samples.summary: Accepted-but-real behavior regression against Google Sheets parity: on the cell the unset fires on, a user-chosen `nf: 'number'` (and its grouping separators, '1,234.5' → '1234.5') is dropped along with `dp`, because nothing records who wrote `nf`. It is documented as a Known deviation in the todo and in sheet-style.md, so it is approved scope, but it means increase/decrease can now remove formatting the buttons never set — flagging so the trade-off is consciously re-confirmed rather than inherited from the todo.

samples.summary: selectionTargets() codifies a pattern already inlined twice nearby (setRangeStyle sheet.ts:3736, resetRangeStyleToDefault sheet.ts:3757) without folding those copies into it, leaving three spellings of the same rule.

selectionRendersAt / the cell scan in unsetRangeStyleValues call store.getGrid over the full selection on every decimal click; for a select-all selection that is a whole-sheet scan per button press, which is a heavier cost than the previous single-patch write. Likely acceptable if getGrid is sparse-populated, but it is a new per-click full-selection read in an interactive path.

finding.summary: New clamp makes Decrease at zero destructive when `dp` is stored, breaking the issue's "equal increases and decreases leave the selection exactly as they found it" rule
finding.evidence: The delta replaces `if (target < 0) return;` with `if (dp + delta < 0 && !explicitDp) return;` plus `const target = Math.max(0, dp + delta)`. So when a cell has an explicitly stored `dp: 0` and the value's own precision is also 0 (e.g. `1234` styled `{dp: 0, nf: 'number'}` from the toolbar), pressing Decrease — which the user reads as a no-op at the floor — now takes the `target === valueDp && explicitDp` branch and unsets `{dp, nf}`, dropping the number format and its grouping separators (`1,234` → `1234`). Pressing Increase afterwards does not restore it: it writes `{dp: 1, nf: 'number'}`. One Decrease + one Increase therefore leaves the cell in a different state than it started, which is exactly the reversibility criterion in docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5 and docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:213-216. Before this delta the same click was an unconditional no-op. It also makes Decrease-at-zero behave differently depending on invisible state (stored vs inferred `dp`), which neither the design doc nor the "Known deviations" list records.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that with a stored `dp: 0` a Decrease now falls into the unset branch and strips `{dp, nf}`. The implementation contains an explicit `!clamped` guard on that branch (sheet.ts:4206-4214): `const clamped = stepped < 0; const target = clamped ? 0 : stepped;` and the unset requires `explicitDp && !clamped && target === valueDp && selectionRendersAt(target)`. For the reviewer's own example (`1234` with `{dp: 0, nf: 'number'}`, delta -1): `stepped = -1`, `explicitDp` true so no early return, `clamped` true, so the unset is skipped and `setRangeStyle({dp: 0})` runs — a merge patch (mergeStylePatch, sheet.ts:3695+), leaving `nf: 'number'` and its separators intact. So Decrease-at-floor is non-destructive and the reversibility criterion is not broken. The claim that the behavior is undocumented is also false: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:225-228 and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:89-92 both record the clamped-step deviation, and packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:104-117 pins it. There is only one `changeDecimals` implementation (view handlers are wrappers), so no alternate unguarded path exists.

finding.summary: `inheritable` gate narrows the spec'd unset rule, so non-plain/number formats keep residue. The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:50-53) specifies: `target === valueDp` and `explicitDp` → try to unset, using `['dp','nf']` when `nf === 'number'` and **`['dp']` otherwise**. The implementation instead only attempts an unset when `!nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'`, so a `currency`/`percent`/date-formatted cell with an explicit `dp` never returns to inheritance: e.g. currency cell holding `12.34` (valueDp 2, default dp 2) → Increase writes `dp: 3` → Decrease targets 2 === valueDp but is blocked by `inheritable`, storing `dp: 2` residue instead of unsetting. That is the same residue class the issue's outcome ("leave a cell exactly as it started") is about, just for a different number format.
finding.evidence: const inheritable = !nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'number'; if (explicitDp && target === valueDp && inheritable) { ... }

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence does not exist. `grep -r inheritable` matches nothing under packages/sheets/src (only slides/board files). `Sheet.changeDecimals` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4209-4224) gates the unset on `explicitDp && !clamped && target === valueDp && selectionRendersAt(target)` with no number-format term, and picks keys exactly as the todo specifies (todo:56-57): `nf === 'number' ? { dp, nf } : { dp }` at sheet.ts:4219-4220. A currency/percent cell with an explicit `dp` therefore does reach the unset path with `{dp}`, and `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4287-4331) refuses only on ownership/value conflicts, not on `nf`. The reviewer's currency `12.34` walkthrough is contradicted by the actual control flow, so the alleged residue class is not present.
